question: A Class M learner's permit allows a rider to operate a motorcycle:
choice_a: At any hour, day or night
explanation: A Class M permit allows you to drive only between sunrise and sunset.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: According to the manual, a Class M learner may carry a passenger only if that passenger is:
choice_b: A family member of any age
choice_d: Anyone, as long as a helmet is worn
explanation: Class M learners shall not carry any passengers other than a properly licensed instructor.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: To earn a Class M license, the manual says an applicant must pass:
choice_b: A knowledge test and an on-cycle skill test
choice_d: A written essay on road safety
explanation: To earn your license, you must pass a knowledge test and an on-cycle skill test.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: The manual says knowledge test questions are based on:
choice_a: State police accident reports from the past year
choice_b: The owner's manual of the specific motorcycle used for testing
choice_c: Information, practices, and ideas from the Motorcycle Operator Manual
explanation: Knowledge test questions are based on information, practices, and ideas from this manual. They require that you know and understand road rules and safe riding practices.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: If you test for your license on a motorcycle that is 5 brake horsepower or less, the manual says your license will carry:
choice_a: A '9' restriction, prohibiting operation of a two-wheeled motorcycle
choice_c: A restriction limiting you to daytime riding only
choice_d: An '8' restriction, prohibiting operation of a motorcycle over 5 brake horsepower
explanation: If you test on a motorcycle that is 5 brake horsepower or less, an '8' restriction will appear on your motorcycle license, prohibiting you from operating a motorcycle of more than 5 brake horsepower.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: If you test for your license on a motorcycle with more than two wheels, the manual says a '9' restriction on your license means you:
choice_a: Are prohibited from operating a two-wheeled motorcycle
choice_b: Are prohibited from operating any motorcycle with a passenger
choice_c: Must retake the test within one year
choice_d: May only ride during daylight hours
explanation: If you test on a motorcycle that has more than 2 wheels, a '9' restriction will appear on your driver's license, prohibiting you from operating a two-wheeled motorcycle.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: Riders under 18 must wait a mandatory period from their permit issue date, and have a signed Certificate of Completion for 65 hours of skill-building, before taking the road test. How long is that mandatory wait?
choice_d: There is no mandatory wait for any applicant
explanation: If you are under 18, you must wait the mandatory 6 months from your permit issue date and have a signed Certificate of Completion for the 65 hours of skill-building before taking your road test.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: The manual says the 15 hours of training obtained through the Basic Rider Course can be used toward:
choice_a: A reduction in the licensing fee
choice_c: Meeting counts toward the 65 hours of skill-building requirement for riders under 18
explanation: The 15 hours of training obtained through the Basic Rider Course can be utilized in meeting counts toward the 65 hours of skill-building requirement.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: According to the manual, how many times may a person reapply for a motorcycle learner's permit within a five-year period?
choice_d: No more than three times (four total permits within five years)
explanation: You may reapply for a motorcycle learner's permit no more than three times in a five-year period (four total learner's permits within five years), and with each reapply, you must successfully pass the motorcycle knowledge test.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), p.39, 'Earning Your License'

question: According to the manual, permit holders who successfully complete the Basic Rider Course will:
choice_b: Still need to separately schedule a skills test at a Driver License Center
choice_c: Only receive a certificate with no effect on licensing
choice_d: Be required to retake the course annually
explanation: The Basic Rider Course lasts 15 hours and is suitable for beginners and intermediate/advanced riders; students on a learner's permit who successfully complete the course will be issued a motorcycle license.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), back cover, 'Free Rider Training Courses for Pennsylvania Residents'

question: According to the manual, a permit holder who completes the 3-Wheel Basic Rider Course on their own 3-wheel motorcycle will be issued a motorcycle license with:
choice_b: A '9' restriction, prohibiting operation of a two-wheel motorcycle
choice_d: A restriction requiring a passenger on every ride
explanation: The 3-Wheel Basic Rider Course is similar to the Basic Rider Course except training is completed on a 3-wheel motorcycle. Students on a learner's permit who successfully complete it will be issued a license with a '9' restriction, prohibiting operation of a two-wheel motorcycle.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), back cover, 'Free Rider Training Courses for Pennsylvania Residents'

question: The manual describes the Advanced Rider Course as a one-day course for experienced, already-licensed riders that:
choice_a: Is required before every license renewal
choice_b: Issues a new Class M license upon completion
choice_d: Replaces the need for the knowledge test
explanation: The Advanced Rider Course is a one-day course geared toward experienced riders who already have their motorcycle license, providing rider development in risk management and decision-making. It is not a licensing course.
source_note: PennDOT Motorcycle Operator Manual (Pub 147, 11-24), back cover, 'Free Rider Training Courses for Pennsylvania Residents'
